items.q:
Sheet layout: A = Code, B = Item, C = Price.

A2 P101 | B2 Bolt | C2 250
A3 P102 | B3 Nut  | C3 300
A4 P103 | B4 Clamp| C4 450

What does =VLOOKUP("P103", B2:C4, 2, FALSE) return?
items.explain: VLOOKUP searches only the first column of the given range; B2:C4 starts at the Item column, so the code P103 is never found.

items.q:
Data (A = Region, B = Product, C = Sales):

North | Bolt | 120
South | Bolt | 80
North | Nut  | 50
North | Bolt | 30

What does =SUMIFS(C:C, A:A, "North", B:B, "Bolt") return?
items.explain: Only rows matching both criteria are summed: 120 + 30 = 150; 200 is all North rows and 230 is all Bolt rows.

items.q: Cell C2 contains =B2*$F$1, where F1 holds the GST rate. You copy C2 and paste it into C3. What formula appears in C3?
items.explain: The relative reference B2 shifts down one row, while the $ signs lock F1 in place so every row uses the same rate.

items.q: A1:A6 contains the marks 45, 78, 92, 60, 88, 35. What does =COUNTIF(A1:A6, ">=60") return?
items.explain: 78, 92, 60 and 88 satisfy the condition; 60 itself counts because the operator is >= not >.

items.q:
B2 contains 60. What does this return?

=IF(B2>=75, "Distinction", IF(B2>=60, "First", "Pass"))
items.explain: The outer test fails (60 < 75), the inner test passes (60 >= 60), so the nested IF returns "First".

items.q: You want a pivot table showing total sales for each Region as rows and each Month as columns. Where does the Sales field go?
items.explain: Rows and Columns hold the categories you group by; the number being aggregated goes into Values, where you choose Sum, Count or Average.

items.q:
A2:A4 = P101, P102, P103 and C2:C4 = 250, 300, 450.

What does =INDEX(C2:C4, MATCH("P102", A2:A4, 0)) return?
items.explain: MATCH finds P102 at position 2, and INDEX returns the second value in C2:C4, which is 300; 2 alone is only the MATCH result.

items.q: A tiffin service sells each box at ₹250 with a variable cost of ₹150 per box. Fixed costs are ₹2 lakh per month. How many boxes per month to break even?
items.explain: Contribution per box = 250 - 150 = ₹100, so break-even = 2,00,000 / 100 = 2,000 boxes; dividing by price or cost instead gives the wrong numbers.

items.q: Opening cash on 1 April is ₹5 lakh. During April, receipts are ₹3.2 lakh and payments are ₹4.5 lakh. What is the closing cash?
items.explain: Closing = opening + receipts - payments = 5 + 3.2 - 4.5 = ₹3.7 lakh; the month's net outflow is 1.3 lakh.

items.q: A product line has revenue of ₹12 lakh and cost of goods sold of ₹9 lakh. What is the gross margin percentage?
items.explain: Gross margin = (12 - 9) / 12 = 25% of revenue; 33.3% is the markup on cost, a different measure.

items.q:
A2:A4 = P101, P102, P103 and C2:C4 = 250, 300, 450.

What does =XLOOKUP("P105", A2:A4, C2:C4, "Not found") return?
items.explain: XLOOKUP's fourth argument is the if-not-found value, so a missing code returns that text instead of the #N/A that VLOOKUP would give.
